definition: Structure from motion (SfM) is a photogrammetric range imaging technique for estimating three-dimensional structures from two-dimensional image sequences that may be coupled with local motion signals.
details: It is a classic problem studied in the fields of computer vision and visual perception. In computer vision, the problem of SfM is to design an algorithm to perform this task. In visual perception, the problem of SfM is to find an algorithm by which biological creatures perform this task.

explainer.lead: Structure from motion estimates three-dimensional structure from two-dimensional image sequences, possibly combined with local motion signals. It matters as a classic problem in computer vision and visual perception, underpinning 3D reconstruction from ordinary images.

tiers.eli5: Like working out the shape of a room by walking around it and comparing how the views change.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers design algorithms that recover 3D structure and camera motion from image sequences. Pitfall: the problem is ill-posed from limited or noisy views, so reconstructions can be unstable.
tiers.paperLevel: A photogrammetric range imaging technique for estimating three-dimensional structures from two-dimensional image sequences, which may be coupled with local motion signals. It is a classic problem in computer vision, where the task is to design such an algorithm, and in visual perception, where the task is to find the algorithm biological creatures use.

explainer.example: Photographs of a building taken from many angles are fed to an SfM pipeline that estimates camera positions and a 3D point cloud of the facade.
